name: Agincourt, The Arrow Storm
summary: Henry V's English army of approximately 6,000-9,000 men defeats a French army estimated at 12,000-36,000 at Agincourt (Azincourt) on October 25, 1415. English longbowmen, positioned with forest flanks and sharpened stakes against cavalry, devastate the compressed French men-at-arms struggling through muddy ground. French casualties include over 6,000 dead, including the Constable of France and three dukes; English dead number in the hundreds.

_quarry.structural_significance: Agincourt is the last and greatest demonstration of the longbow's tactical supremacy; its outcome directly enables the Treaty of Troyes (1420) making Henry V heir to France; the slaughter of the French nobility creates a power vacuum that the Armagnac-Burgundian conflict fills, weakening French resistance; Henry V's death two years later shows that military genius alone cannot create permanent dynastic change
